method: Condition independent weighted Bernoulli edges on acyclicity; factor disjoint cycle constraints in cactus graphs
result: Complete author-checked proof of negative association for all finite cactus graphs and finite positive edge weights; target on arbitrary graphs remains unsolved here
independent_check: Direct subset counts for uniform cycles give covariance -2^(m-2)/(2^m-1)^2; triangle -2/49 and tree zero agree
failed_route_counterexample: Fair bits conditioned to avoid X1X2=X2X3=1 have allowed states 000,100,010,001,101 and Cov(X1,X3)=1/25>0
obstruction: Overlapping cycle constraints do not factor; generic conditioning on a decreasing event fails. Need an inequality using graphic-matroid circuit elimination.

independent_check: Walks avoiding the neighboring root inject by prepending; walks visiting it inject into reversed-prefix/suffix pairs. These are disjoint cases and preserve lengths.
method: Adjacent-root walk decomposition and a Markov/Borel-Cantelli bound
obstruction: The cut-walk inequality has an environment-dependent endpoint maximum. No stationary scalar subadditive process or liminf lower bound was obtained.
result: Root-independent limsup on every infinite connected bounded-degree graph; annealed upper bound p mu

independent_check: Two-state cyclic example checks the pushforward direction and normalization; finite-window rejection sampling gives an independent special-case construction
method: Forward density matching on the ergodic two-sided Wiener shift
obstruction: No mathematical gap currently identified under the stated interpretation; source interpretation, measurability details, and earlier filling/embedding literature still under review
result: Complete candidate construction of a finite nonnegative integer prefix time for any suffix law absolutely continuous with respect to Wiener measure

independent_check: Exact second-moment recursion proves color measurability; full conditional subtree law proves stationarity; source definition expressly permits zero child weights
method: Endogenous AND/OR tree coloring and conditional subtree selection
obstruction: No mathematical gap currently identified; full author recheck and prior tree-automaton literature pending
result: Candidate counterexample: GW itself stationary, with two invariant color classes of mass one half

independent_check: The example is a real sequence, not a self-avoiding-walk counterexample. The square-root subadditivity checks the claimed property directly.
method: Submultiplicativity and its limits
obstruction: Submultiplicativity cannot determine the critical exponent or the dimension-four logarithmic correction.
result: On Z^d, splitting a walk gives c_(m+n)<=c_m c_n. Positive-coordinate walks give d^n<=c_n, and the nonbacktracking bound gives c_n<=2d(2d-1)^(n-1). Fekete determines the exponential growth rate. However a_n=mu^n exp(sqrt(n)) is submultiplicative and has no fixed polynomial prefactor.

independent_check: The endpoint stays in the graph; deleting it would invalidate the argument. Fixed-length conditioning also fixes the remaining length and is a different ensemble.
method: Exact finite-domain conditional law
obstruction: This domain Markov property supplies neither tightness nor conformal invariance and does not identify an SLE scaling limit.
result: For a finite-graph a-to-b self-avoiding path with weight z^length, condition on an initial simple prefix. The remaining path has the same fugacity law on the graph with earlier prefix vertices removed. The factor z^prefix_length cancels between numerator and partition function.

independent_check: The finite-state bijection proves the torus assertion independently of sampling. The straight-run bound tends to zero for each fixed p>0.
method: Invertible routing and finite-volume diagnostics
obstruction: Finite periodic loop counts cannot decide infinite-volume escape; the N-to-infinity and p-to-zero limits cannot be interchanged from this bound.
result: The local mirror pairings define an invertible map on oriented light states. Its orbits are cycles or bi-infinite trajectories. On a finite periodic torus every orbit is a cycle. A mirror-free initial straight run of N sites has probability (1-p)^N.

independent_check: The factor is total mirror length, not half-length. Parallel mirrors contribute zero area and endpoint coincidences have zero intensity. The rate is positive for every alpha if mu is not concentrated on a single unoriented direction.
method: Exact first-collision distribution for Poisson mirrors
obstruction: After reflection, previously examined empty regions and previously hit mirrors make the flight history dependent. The first-flight computation gives no independent-flight construction or escape threshold.
result: For a straight test ray segment of length L in direction alpha and mirrors of total length epsilon with orientation law mu, the centers whose mirror crosses the segment form a parallelogram of area epsilon L |sin(alpha-beta)| for angle beta. Unit-intensity marked Poisson counting gives no-collision probability exp(-epsilon L integral |sin(alpha-beta)| mu(dbeta)). Thus the first free flight is exponential whenever this rate is positive.

independent_check: The corridor is only a counterexample to the topological inference. It is not asserted to be a configuration of the source mirror model.
method: Attempted reduction to straight visibility
obstruction: Unboundedness of the vacant component gives a continuous route, not a realizable billiard route. No mirror configuration trapping all angles, or theorem preventing one, was constructed.
result: An unbounded unobstructed straight ray from the origin immediately rules out the proposed all-directions trapped configuration. However an unbounded connected planar open set need not contain any unbounded straight ray: a sufficiently narrow unbounded spiral corridor is a topological counterexample to that inference.

independent_check: Conditioning on A proves the mixture limit; its fourth moment differs from that of a Gaussian with the same variance. This is not a unit-speed mirror-model counterexample.
method: Green-Kubo variance and a failed CLT shortcut
obstruction: Need mixing or a martingale approximation for the billiard environment, including the effect of conditioning on an unbounded trajectory.
result: For a stationary mean-zero scalar velocity with integrable covariance C(s), Var(integral_0^t V_s ds)/t = 2 integral_0^t (1-s/t) C(s) ds tends to 2 integral_0^infinity C(s) ds. Covariance control alone does not imply a Gaussian limit: let Y_i=A epsilon_i with independent fair signs and independent A equal to 1 or 2 with probability 1/2. Distinct increments are uncorrelated, but n^(-1/2) sum Y_i converges to the equally weighted mixture of N(0,1) and N(0,4).

independent_check: The finite-run probability agrees with independence and has the correct q=0 endpoint. Adding a mirror changes routing rather than merely deleting traversable states, so an edgewise percolation monotonicity proof has not been supplied.
method: Small-density straight paths and lack of an order argument
obstruction: The known localization interval near and above one-half cannot be extended to every q>0 using this finite-run bound or an unproved monotonicity assumption.
result: At q=0 a ray moves indefinitely along its Manhattan street. The event that its first N potential collisions contain no mirror has probability (1-q)^N. This only controls a finite initial flight and gives no positive lower bound as N increases at fixed q.

independent_check: The comparison is inclusion of path events, not equality of the two models. It proves a region above the directed-percolation threshold and its reflected counterpart only.
method: Directed-percolation subgraph comparison
obstruction: It does not settle the interval between one-half and that threshold. The critical p=1/2 result does not extend by continuity alone.
result: Reflecting both coordinate axes maps p to 1-p, so the infinite-path probability is symmetric about one-half. North-east paths use independent edges pointing north/east with probability p; survival of the usual north-east directed percolation therefore implies survival in the full oriented graph. The p=0 and p=1 endpoints have deterministic infinite paths.

independent_check: Check both timelines: C remains infectious at 9 in each case; A has already died at 1 only in the baseline. The example refutes infection-set inclusion under scaled lifetimes on a fixed contact schedule.
method: Counterexample to the usual pathwise lifetime monotonicity coupling
obstruction: This is not a counterexample to survival monotonicity or to the Brownian epidemic conjecture. It blocks a direct attractiveness proof; a Brownian contact-support realization was not proved.
result: Consider a deterministic contact schedule with A initially infected: A-C at time .1, A-B at 1, C-B at 9, B-D at 10, and no other contacts. Baseline infectious lifetimes are L_A=.5, L_C=12, L_B=2. Then B is infected at 9 and infects D at 10. Multiply every lifetime by 3: A now infects B at 1; B is removed at 7, cannot be reinfected at 9, and D is never infected.

independent_check: The upper bound follows by the exponential-moment union bound and minimizing its parameter; coordinate vectors prove the norm identity even for even r by taking absolute value outside the form.
method: Diagonal-tensor Gaussian estimate
obstruction: This verifies a restricted diagonal family. Off-diagonal terms and the full p range require the tensor geometry absent here.
result: For a diagonal homogeneous form T(x)=sum_j a_j x_j^r and 2<=p<=r, its supremum over the l_p unit ball is max_j |a_j|. Indeed sum |x_j|^r<=1 and a coordinate vector attains the maximum. For independent standard g_i, each diagonal coefficient of sum_i g_i T_i has variance at most sum_i ||T_i||^2, so the Gaussian maximum bound gives E||sum_i g_i T_i|| <= sqrt(2 log(2d)) (sum_i ||T_i||^2)^(1/2).

independent_check: The example has a symmetric law and exp(Z_n) in [n^(-1/2),n^(1/2)]. Its expectation is 1-1/sqrt(n)+(1+n^(-1))/(2), which tends to 3/2. It is not a random-graph construction.
method: Complement symmetry and uniform-integrability obstruction
obstruction: Need a sharp upper bound and uniform integrability at the sqrt(n) scale; complement symmetry only yields the lower bound.
result: The theta product inequality theta(G) theta(complement G)>=n and complement symmetry of G(n,1/2) give E theta>=sqrt(n) by arithmetic-geometric mean. A proof of concentration on a logarithmic scale would still need tail control: set Z_n to plus or minus (log n)/2, each with probability 1/(2 sqrt(n)), and zero otherwise. Then Z_n tends to zero in probability and variance, but E exp(Z_n) tends to 3/2.

independent_check: The exact identity is stronger than the general product inequality. The symmetric rare-tail example in P0013 has Z tending to zero in probability yet E cosh Z tending to 3/2, so concentration alone is insufficient.
method: Vertex-transitive complement identity
obstruction: Must estimate the exponential tails of the logarithmic theta fluctuation for the dependent circulant adjacency structure.
result: A circulant graph is vertex transitive, so theta(G) theta(complement G)=n. Its random model is complement invariant. For Z=log(theta(G)/sqrt(n)), Z has the law of -Z and E theta/sqrt(n)=E cosh Z. The conjecture is therefore equivalent to E(cosh Z-1) tending to zero.

independent_check: Dimension gives a nonzero H without assuming generic rank three; the spanning condition rules out semidefinite kernel elements. Spectral decomposition independently verifies equal squared magnitudes.
method: Complete M=2 obstruction via Hermitian lifting
obstruction: For M>2 a nonzero kernel matrix need not have rank at most two with one eigenvalue of each sign. The requisite low-rank intersection probability remains unresolved.
result: For M=2 the matrix has three complex Gaussian rows. Almost surely these span C^2. The real-linear measurement map from the four-dimensional Hermitian 2-by-2 space to R^3 has a nonzero kernel element H. H cannot be positive or negative semidefinite: a_i^* H a_i=0 for a spanning set would force H=0. Thus H has one positive and one negative eigenvalue and can be written xx^*-yy^* with noncollinear x,y. Their three intensity measurements agree. Hence p_2=0.

independent_check: Full spark holds almost surely. Adding rows increases the Gram matrix, so the minimum relevant frame bound is attained among M-row subsets. Both bounds use union/inclusion inequalities and never assume independence among overlapping minors.
method: Union small-ball lower bound and one-normal upper bound
obstruction: The exponential lower bound and polynomial upper bound are far apart. Sharp extremes of the strongly dependent minors remain uncontrolled.
result: For a standard M-by-M real Gaussian matrix A, sigma_min(A)<=t implies that some column has distance at most sqrt(M)t from the span of the other columns: project a minimizing unit vector equation using a coordinate of magnitude at least 1/sqrt(M). Each such distance has the law |N(0,1)|, so P(sigma_min<=t)<=sqrt(2/pi) M^(3/2)t. There are at most 4^M M-row submatrices of a (2M-1)-by-M frame. Therefore its minimum omega exceeds exp(-(log 4+epsilon)M) with probability tending to one. Conversely fix M-1 rows and a unit normal u. The M remaining row projections are independent N(0,1), and omega is at most their minimum absolute value, giving omega<=C log(M)/M with probability tending to one for sufficiently large C.

independent_check: The constant is attained by any nonconstant linear function, checking both normalization and dimension independence.
method: Gaussian special case by orthogonal expansion
obstruction: A general isotropic log-concave measure lacks this diagonal Hermite generator. This special case does not prove its uniform Poincare or Cheeger bound.
result: For standard Gaussian measure, expand a polynomial f in orthonormal multivariate Hermite polynomials with coefficients a_alpha. Then Var(f)=sum_(|alpha|>=1) a_alpha^2 <= sum |alpha| a_alpha^2 = E||gradient f||^2. Closure in Gaussian Sobolev norm extends the inequality to its natural domain.

independent_check: Orthogonality concerns equality of edge monomials, not equality of vertex labelings. Distinct labelings can produce the same edge set and must not be discarded.
method: Moment expansion with a crude operator-norm bound
obstruction: The Frobenius bound can lose powers of n and cannot decide the sharp operator norm or the existence of one power-log asymptotic form.
result: For every finite random graph matrix, E||M|| <= (E||M||_F^2)^(1/2). Expanding each entry as a sum of Rademacher edge monomials, cross terms vanish unless the two monomials use every edge with even combined multiplicity. For a fixed shape the remaining label identifications can be counted to obtain a polynomial upper bound in n.

independent_check: The sign is checked on a half-space, where the vector from an interior point to the exit point has positive outward-normal component.
method: Smooth-boundary directional containment
obstruction: Containment does not prove that all hemisphere directions occur, and there is no supporting tangent half-space at the arbitrary boundaries in the full question.
result: At an exit point z where the domain boundary is C^1 with outward unit normal n, local differentiability gives n dot (z-x)>=-o(|z-x|) for x in the domain approaching z. Thus every limit of (z-B_s)/|z-B_s| as s increases to the exit time lies in the closed hemisphere {u:n dot u>=0}.

independent_check: A closure contact alone does not ensure an accessible common boundary point. This is why the necessary finite-chain condition was not promoted to an equivalence.
method: Reduction to component adjacency and access
obstruction: Need finite accessible chains for every pair of components, simultaneously for the Brownian trace.
result: If both endpoints lie in the same component of the complement of the Brownian trace, an open connected planar set is polygonally connected; removing loops gives a simple arc avoiding the trace entirely. If an arc crosses the trace finitely many times, its complementary intervals give a finite sequence of complement components with touching closures at successive crossing points.

independent_check: The restriction is onto because every value of the Cantor function is attained on the Cantor set, including plateau values at endpoints.
method: Failure of transferring total disconnectedness through the path map
obstruction: The spatial remainder needs direct Brownian geometry. Showing it contains no simple arc would also be weaker than showing every connected component is a singleton.
result: A possible approach is to identify a totally disconnected set of Brownian times surviving boundary removal. That would not suffice: the Cantor function restricted to the middle-third Cantor set maps this totally disconnected compact set continuously onto [0,1]. Continuous images can be connected.

independent_check: This argument does not require rectifiability or a parametrized simple curve, and hence applies to the connectivity notion in a percolation-dimension lower bound.
method: Universal dimension lower bound for connecting sets
obstruction: Polygonal approximations of a Brownian path are not subsets of its trace. The missing step is constructing sufficiently thin connecting subsets inside the trace itself.
result: Any connected set containing distinct x and y has Hausdorff dimension at least one. Orthogonal projection onto their joining line is Lipschitz and has connected image containing the interval between the projections, so its dimension is at least one.

independent_check: The exponent is the eigenvalue of the actual reflected-Brownian generator: using Delta rather than Delta/2 changes it by a factor of two.
method: Spectral lower bound on coupling tails
obstruction: This proves that the spectral rate is an upper limit on coupling efficiency, but gives no coupling attaining arbitrarily close to that rate in an acute triangle.
result: Let phi be a bounded nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction with semigroup P_t phi=e^(-lambda t) phi. For any coalescent coupling with meeting time T, |P_t phi(x)-P_t phi(y)|<=2||phi||_infinity P(T>t). Choosing phi(x)!=phi(y) yields P(T>t)>=c e^(-lambda t).

independent_check: Each sign follows from the supporting half-space inequality at the boundary point. The calculation uses finite-variation reflection terms and has no missing quadratic-variation term.
method: Synchronous contraction on convex domains
obstruction: Nonincrease alone does not prove convergence to zero. Nonconvex domains can have both signs and require control of the long-run reflection geometry.
result: For two reflected motions driven by the same Brownian path, the noise cancels in their difference. With inward normals, d|X-Y|^2=2<X-Y,n(X)>dL_X-2<X-Y,n(Y)>dL_Y. Convexity makes both contributions nonpositive, so the distance is nonincreasing.

independent_check: Both test locations lie in the exterior and the normal points into that same domain, fixing the otherwise easy sign error.
method: Exterior-disk reflection has both distance signs
obstruction: A global monotone-distance proof is unavailable. The question turns on boundary occupation and angular correlations over indefinitely long times.
result: At x=(R,0) on the inner circular boundary of the exterior domain, its inward-to-domain normal is (1,0). For y=(r,0), r>R, <x-y,n>=R-r<0; for y=(-r,0) it is R+r>0. Hence a reflection at X can either shrink or enlarge the synchronous separation.

independent_check: The known N=2 result is excluded from this target. A pair comparison does not transfer automatically to N>=3 because a particle can clone the third particle rather than its proposed comparator.
method: Attempted boundary-distance Lyapunov proof
obstruction: No Lyapunov drift bound uniform over arbitrary boundary geometry and all cloning configurations was obtained.
result: The candidate Lyapunov function -sum_i log dist(X_i,boundary D) becomes singular when particles approach the boundary, but an Ito argument needs derivative bounds. Even for a smooth domain, the distance is nonsmooth on its medial set; for arbitrary domains there may be no uniformly controlled smooth substitute. At a cloning event another particle may be still closer to the boundary, so the jump is not uniformly favorable.

independent_check: The annulus excludes the origin; a disk would have zero minimum displacement and would not satisfy this check.
method: Explicit deterministic shy coupling on an annulus
obstruction: This verifies a nonempty deterministic class. It does not turn an arbitrary shy coupling into a single state map with the required path consistency.
result: If an isometry F preserves a reflected-Brownian domain and has inf_x |x-F(x)|>0, take Y_t=F(X_t). Orthogonal transformation of Brownian noise and equivariance of inward reflection show Y has the correct reflected law, while separation stays positive. On R<|x|<R_out, F(x)=-x yields |X_t-Y_t|>=2R.

independent_check: For each deterministic s, {s<T} is measurable from the segment up to s. Future Brownian increments followed by independent stopped segments retain the Brownian law and are independent of the past. Integrating over s gives a Brownian future under Q; stationarity then supplies a Brownian past and its independence. This is a proof outline pending full artifact and earlier-literature comparison, not a newly claimed theorem.
method: Stationary Palm construction in the identically distributed finite-mean case
obstruction: The actual question allows independent non-identically distributed segments. There is then no invariant iid index law or common Palm mean to which this argument applies.
result: For iid stopped Brownian segments with 0<E T<infinity, the cycle sequence is ergodic under shifting its index. A stationary occupation law is Q(F)=E[integral_0^T F(theta_s X) ds]/E T. Shifting by t changes the numerator by E[integral_T^(T+t) F(theta_s X) ds-integral_0^t F(theta_s X) ds]=0 because the concatenation rooted at the next cycle has the same Palm law. Tilting the iid cycle sequence by T_0/E T and choosing a uniform time in that cycle realizes this law; the forward filling lemma supplies that tilt by a finite randomized index shift.

independent_check: Adjacent vertices cannot both be peaks. In the four-cycle, a proposed peak with label 2 would have to exceed both other nonpeak labels, which is impossible; this checks the count without enumeration software.
method: Exact small-grid count and an orientation reformulation
obstruction: The small-grid calculation gives no large-n scale. The orientation sum requires sharp weighted counts of acyclic orientations with two prescribed sinks. The source title says repel while its displayed question asks distance/n -> 0; that wording discrepancy is retained, not silently corrected.
result: On the 2-by-2 grid (a four-cycle), exactly two peaks must be opposite and carry labels 3 and 4. There are two choices of diagonal, two orders of the top labels, and two orders of the bottom labels: eight of the 24 labelings. Their graph distance is always two. More generally orient each edge toward its larger label. Two peaks means precisely two sinks of the induced acyclic orientation; the number of labelings yielding a fixed orientation is its number of linear extensions.

independent_check: Independence of two halves at a proposed joining time is insufficient if their Brownian marginal laws have been lost there.
method: Common-splice compatibility obstruction
obstruction: No construction aligns both certificates at one time while preserving both marginal laws and their independence.
result: Two independent standard Brownian half-paths attached at the same deterministic time give a two-sided Brownian motion. For a general process certified separately as forward and backward Brownian, the certifying random times can differ. Moving either certificate to another random time can bias its marginal law, as the selection-density calculation in P0032 demonstrates.

independent_check: Independence is not needed for this Borel-Cantelli upper bound. Infinite means do not contradict the almost-sure sparse-clock estimate.
method: Sparse exceptional hitting-time clock estimate
obstruction: A negligible exceptional time fraction is an asymptotic statement; it does not construct an exact backward Brownian law after a finite random shift. The full frequency classification remains open here.
result: For a standard Brownian first hitting time tau of -1, reflection gives P(tau>t)=2 Phi(1/sqrt(t))-1 ~ sqrt(2/pi)t^(-1/2), hence E tau=infinity. If exceptional segment indices are 2^k, then sum_k P(tau_k>epsilon 2^k)<infinity. Borel-Cantelli yields tau_k/2^k ->0 almost surely. Splitting the sum into finitely many early terms and a geometrically weighted tail gives sum_(k<=K) tau_k/2^K ->0.

independent_check: The predictable quadratic variation of the horizontal coordinate counts first visits, and the vertical one counts repeat visits; their sum is exactly n.
method: Martingale estimates for the axis-switching walk
obstruction: Zero speed and a diffusive second moment do not imply recurrence. The occupation-dependent balance of the two coordinate clocks remains uncontrolled.
result: The axis of the next step is predictable from the past, while its sign is fair. Both coordinates are martingales, their cross quadratic covariation is zero, and E|X_n|^2=n. Bounded increments and Azuma give summable bounds for P(|X_n|>epsilon n), so X_n/n tends to zero almost surely.

independent_check: The speed tends to zero at lambda=b and to one at lambda=0, checking the normalization.
method: Exact radial speed on a regular tree
obstruction: General Cayley graphs have dead ends and nonuniform distance-level neighborhoods. Transience alone does not control time spent in traps.
result: On the (b+1)-regular rooted tree, away from the root the radial walk steps out with probability b/(b+lambda) and in with probability lambda/(b+lambda). For lambda<b its speed is (b-lambda)/(b+lambda)>0: the root is visited finitely often and the bounded-difference martingale law of large numbers applies to the radial drift.

independent_check: At level m the largest attached contribution starts around n=m/2 and has order b^(m/2), up to constant factors and a geometric sum. Every attachment is finite, so no additional infinite ray appears.
method: Equal level growth does not determine branching number
obstruction: This is not a geodesic Cayley spanning-tree counterexample. It proves that matching sphere counts alone cannot establish the conjectured branching number.
result: A geodesic spanning tree has exactly the Cayley graph sphere sizes at each level. But growth can exceed branching number for a bounded-degree tree: take a single infinite spine and at its nth vertex attach a finite b-ary tree of height n. Its level sizes have exponential rate sqrt(b)>1, while its only infinite ray is the spine and arbitrarily deep singleton cutsets give branching number one.

independent_check: There are three equiprobable spanning trees of a triangle, which checks the latter probabilities directly. The determinantal argument is for a positive semidefinite transfer-current kernel.
method: BK for fixed conjunctions and a nonincreasing-event obstruction
obstruction: General increasing disjoint occurrence is a union over adaptive witnesses. A fixed-coordinate negative-association inequality cannot simply be applied after that union.
result: For disjoint fixed edge sets F and H, the spanning-tree determinantal formula and Hadamard-Fischer inequality give P(F union H subset T)<=P(F subset T)P(H subset T). Thus fixed increasing conjunctions obey the desired inequality. The increasing condition matters: on a triangle, A={e in T} and B={f not in T}, e!=f, have disjoint coordinate witnesses but P(A intersection B)=1/3>2/9=P(A)P(B).

independent_check: The root has b+1 possible children but a finite root modification does not change transience. At bp<=1 the nondegenerate branching process dies out.
method: Percolation on regular trees
obstruction: The reduction uses independent descendant trees and does not extend to clusters with overlapping paths in a general transient Cayley graph.
result: For bond percolation on the (b+1)-regular tree, descendants of a nonroot vertex form a Galton-Watson process with Binomial(b,p) offspring. Conditional on survival when bp>1, its branching number is bp almost surely, so the electrical-network branching-number criterion gives transience.

independent_check: Reachability in H implies membership in B_G(x,n), but distances in the exponential bound remain intrinsic to H. Bounded degrees control the prefactor. This is a consequence of the classical heat-kernel bound, not a novelty claim.
method: Zero speed on every bounded-degree subexponential-growth subgraph
obstruction: It settles the zero-speed equivalence for subexponential-growth Cayley graphs and their clusters only. Exponential-growth cases need different information.
result: Let H be a connected subgraph of a bounded-degree graph G with |B_G(x,n)|=exp(o(n)). The Carne-Varopoulos bound gives P_x(X_n=y)<=2 sqrt(deg_H(y)/deg_H(x)) exp(-d_H(x,y)^2/(2n)). Summing over reachable vertices yields P(d_H(x,X_n)>=epsilon n)<=C exp(o(n)-epsilon^2 n/2), which is summable. Thus the intrinsic speed on H is zero almost surely.

independent_check: This use is restricted to Cayley graphs; no unverified extension of the strict-critical-threshold theorem to every quasi-transitive graph is presumed.
method: Amenable Cayley special case and a cutset bottleneck
obstruction: The remaining nonamenable quasi-transitive setting needs bounds on separating cutsets or cycle structure. A bounded cycle-basis argument is unavailable without its hypotheses.
result: For an amenable Cayley graph with one end, uniqueness gives p_u=p_c. The known strict p_c<1 theorem for transitive graphs not roughly isometric to Z therefore gives p_u<1 in this special case. One-endedness excludes the two-ended roughly-Z case.

independent_check: The attachment events can be placed on an infinite collection of disjoint descendant cones. For p<=1/b there is no infinite cluster.
method: Strict gap on regular trees
obstruction: This proves the strict gap in a fundamental nonamenable family. Nonamenability by itself does not provide the same independent cone decomposition.
result: On a (b+1)-regular tree with b>=2, branching-process survival gives p_c=1/b. For every p in (1/b,1), infinitely many separated descendant subtrees contain infinite open clusters while their attachment edge is closed, using independent positive-probability events. Thus there are infinitely many clusters and p_u=1.

independent_check: An infinite bi-infinite path supplies a stable set since each vertex has two vacant neighbors. Finite trees have an exposed leaf and are exhausted by the pruning process. Critical Binomial(2,1/2) clusters die out.
method: Bootstrap thresholds on the line and the three-regular tree
obstruction: This illustrates both the amenable endpoint behavior and a nonamenable interior threshold. It does not classify every generating set or every group.
result: On Z the one-neighbor bootstrap threshold is zero, whereas the two-neighbor threshold is one because any initially vacant adjacent pair stays vacant. On the three-regular tree with threshold two, the final vacant set is the two-core of the initial vacant percolation. If its density q<=1/2, all vacant clusters are finite almost surely and leaf pruning empties them. If q>1/2, with positive probability a vertex has two surviving vacant branches, giving a bi-infinite vacant path that remains vacant. Hence the complete-occupation threshold is p=1/2.

independent_check: The strict inequality can also be obtained from the binomial generating function lying strictly above its tangent at one. This excludes the deterministic b=1 exception, whose p_c is one.
method: Critical branching-process extinction
obstruction: Critical clusters in a general quasi-transitive graph are not independent branching trees. Their loop dependence is not captured by this fixed-point proof.
result: For the regular tree at p=1/b, an infinite descendant cluster would have survival probability x satisfying x=1-(1-px)^b. For b>=2 strict concavity gives 1-(1-x/b)^b<x for every x>0, so only x=0 is possible.

independent_check: The argument averages probability measures, not individual configurations, so convexity preserves the marginals and the monotone support. Compactness is available for a countable locally finite edge set.
method: Invariant monotone coupling under an amenable action
obstruction: For a nonamenable acting group there is no Folner averaging sequence. Existence of an arbitrary monotone coupling does not by itself produce an invariant one.
result: Start with a monotone coupling of the two invariant forest laws under a countable amenable action. Average its translates over a Folner sequence. The product space of two edge configurations is compact, the prescribed marginals are unchanged, and the order relation is closed. A subsequential weak limit is therefore still a monotone coupling and is invariant because translation changes each average by at most its Folner boundary ratio.

independent_check: A finite tree has only one spanning tree, so the free-group calculation is exact and requires no limiting interchange.
method: Rational finite-volume values do not force a rational limit
obstruction: The general finitely presented-group question needs the algebraic structure behind the first l2 Betti number; rationality of finite combinatorial counts is insufficient.
result: For the standard free-group Cayley tree the free spanning forest is the entire tree, so its expected degree is the integer 2r. Finite exhaustion spanning-tree expectations are rational under unit conductances, but rational approximants can converge to an irrational number, as floor(n sqrt(2))/n demonstrates.

independent_check: The root-degree estimate is the finite sum of per-edge addition probabilities. Combined with the known opposite cost inequality, the proposed construction would prove equality, not merely a weak approximation statement.
method: Connection to the cost equality obstruction
obstruction: No dependent sprinkling construction was found. This reduction explains why independent sprinkling or a generic connectivity argument does not settle the question.
result: If the free forest is already connected, taking its own configuration gives the requested extension with no added edges. Otherwise, an invariant connected extension with each edge added with probability at most epsilon would have expected root degree at most E deg_F(o)+deg_G(o) epsilon. The standard invariant-graphing bound would then imply cost(Gamma)<=E deg_F(o)/2=1+beta_1(Gamma) after epsilon tends to zero.

independent_check: The finite edge change can preserve acyclicity when it joins two different tree components, so acyclicity does not remove this obstruction.
method: Why tail triviality alone does not fix the component count
obstruction: A forest-law-specific argument making the count constant is still needed in the absence of a useful invariant ergodic action.
result: An ergodic action under which the forest law is invariant makes its component count deterministic. On an arbitrary network there need not be such an action. Trying to substitute tail triviality fails at the logical step: adding one edge between two components can change the component count, so this statistic has not been shown to be measurable with respect to the edge tail sigma-field.

independent_check: The two components are the even and odd integers; every retained vertex has degree two and neither component contains a cycle.
method: Invariant ergodicity permits a finite component count larger than one
obstruction: This forest is not asserted to have a uniform-spanning-forest law. The target requires extra free-forest structure in the nonunimodular case.
result: On the Cayley graph of Z with generators +/-1 and +/-2, retain exactly the edges of length two. The resulting deterministic spanning forest has two bi-infinite components, is translation invariant, and its point-mass law is ergodic. Thus those two properties alone cannot exclude a finite count of two.

independent_check: An existence statement about some components would remain weaker than the source assertion about every component even if the first step survived.
method: Missing mass-transport step in the nonunimodular case
obstruction: No replacement weighted transport and no counterexample with the required FUSF/WUSF inequality were obtained. This is a failed proof route, not a new theorem.
result: In the unimodular setting, an expected-degree argument can establish the presence of infinitely ended components, and indistinguishability can promote a component property to all components. On a nonunimodular graph the unweighted root mass balance used in that argument is invalid; modular weights enter and light components need not receive the same balance.

independent_check: The singular and absolutely continuous parts are preserved by the action by uniqueness of Lebesgue decomposition; this is the load-bearing invariance step.
method: Distinct invariant ergodic laws are mutually singular
obstruction: This handles forest laws admitting such an ergodic common action. Arbitrary networks may lack it; two distinct probability laws need not be singular in general.
result: For a fixed countable group action, two distinct invariant ergodic probability measures are mutually singular. In the Lebesgue decomposition of one relative to the other, the absolutely continuous part is invariant. Its density is invariant and hence constant under the second ergodic law; ergodicity of the first forces its absolutely continuous mass to be either zero or one. Nonzero overlap therefore forces equality.

independent_check: The added edge creates no cycle and the change is finite. Thus the property can change within the class of spanning forests under a finite edge modification.
method: The all-one-ended event is not automatically a tail event
obstruction: Uniform-forest tail triviality cannot be invoked until a separate tail representation of the event is proved. The example is a logical obstruction, not a uniform-forest counterexample.
result: Take two disjoint one-ended infinite trees and add one edge joining them. Before the addition every component has one end; afterwards the connected tree has two ends, since deleting the joining edge separates two infinite pieces.

independent_check: The elementary sequence of probability laws delta_0,delta_1,delta_0,delta_1 is tight but has no full limit, illustrating precisely the missing implication rather than modeling WUSF bushes.
method: Stationarity along a chosen spine is an additional requirement
obstruction: Need regeneration or asymptotic stationarity along the loop-erased spine. Known high-growth and standard-lattice cases in the source must be removed before claiming a new remaining case.
result: The WUSF viewed from an ordinary invariant root and the WUSF viewed from the nth vertex on its distinguished spine are different rooted laws. Moving along the spine is a configuration-dependent selection and need not preserve the original root law. Compactness or tightness, even if proved for the bush sequence, would only give subsequential limits.

independent_check: The deterministic sequence only disproves the logical inference that every infinite path has a largest label. It is not an iid weighted-graph realization or a counterexample to the wired forest question.
method: A failed largest-edge argument on an infinite path
obstruction: One-endedness needs an invasion-percolation or mass-transport argument that treats unattained suprema and the nonunimodular setting.
result: A finite-cycle minimum-spanning-tree proof deletes the largest edge of a cycle. A proposed extension to a bi-infinite path fails because its supremum need not be attained: labels 1-1/(|k|+2) along k in Z approach one and have no maximum.

independent_check: The free forest statement follows directly from its finite-cycle definition; it is not the wired definition, which also sees connections at infinity.
method: Regular-tree special case and resampling obstruction
obstruction: A minimal forest is not a Bernoulli insertion-tolerant process. Arguments proving end properties for percolation do not transfer without controlling the forced deletions.
result: On a regular tree every edge is a bridge and there are no finite cycles, so the free minimal spanning forest is the whole tree. It has infinitely many ends, providing a direct special case where free and wired forests differ. On a graph with cycles, inserting an edge can force deletion of another edge by the cycle-maximum rule.

independent_check: The condition p_u>p_c is retained; assuming it for every nonamenable graph would silently solve another admitted conjecture. The proposition does not say that one p_u cluster meets only one forest component.
method: The easy direction of the uniqueness connection
obstruction: The reverse direction needs to exclude several free-forest components meeting the same infinite p_u cluster. The stronger component-bijection formulation remains unproved here.
result: Under the p_u>p_c hypothesis in the source proposition, each FMSF component meets exactly one infinite p_u cluster. Consequently a connected FMSF can meet only one such cluster, so connectivity implies uniqueness at p_u in that setting.

independent_check: The example is explicitly not a minimal-spanning-forest law. It separates the zero-one statement for invariant events from a classification of possible constant values.
method: Ergodic factor laws give constancy but not the value of the count
obstruction: The usual insertion-tolerance route must account for cycle-breaking deletions. No argument excluding a finite count between two and infinity was obtained in the full quasi-transitive scope.
result: Minimal spanning forests are equivariant functions of iid continuous edge labels, so an ergodic label action makes their component count constant. That alone permits a finite constant larger than one: the invariant deterministic two-component forest on Z with generators +/-1,+/-2 from P0048 is a counterexample to the purely ergodic inference.

independent_check: The first implication uses only the definition of an invariant spanning tree. The second is explicitly conditional on a separate unproved component correspondence.
method: Conditional implication through the component-bijection conjecture
obstruction: Two properties sharing FMSF disconnection as a consequence do not thereby imply one another. Neither unconditional implication in the source question is established here.
result: If there is no invariant random spanning tree, the invariant FMSF cannot be connected, because a connected spanning forest would itself be such a tree. If the stronger conjecture in P0055 gave a bijection between free-forest components and infinite p_u clusters, that disconnection would imply multiple clusters at p_u.

independent_check: Every vertex belongs to exactly one component and there are no cycles. If full square-lattice automorphism invariance is desired, also choose a uniform horizontal/vertical orientation; the full automorphism group is transitive on the resulting finite orbit.
method: Invariant ergodicity does not imply component indistinguishability
obstruction: This is not a minimal-spanning-forest construction. It disproves only the shortcut from invariance and ergodicity to indistinguishability.
result: Construct a periodic forest on Z^2 using blocks of four horizontal rows. The first row is a bi-infinite horizontal path. The next three rows form a comb: the middle row is a horizontal spine, with each vertex in the two outer rows attached vertically to that spine. Repeat and choose a uniformly random vertical phase. The law is translation invariant and ergodic on its finite phase orbit, yet its components are distinguishable as lines and combs by the existence of degree-four vertices.

independent_check: A convergent subsequence of bush laws would not establish a full limit. The period-two sequence example in P0052 shows the logical distinction.
method: Unique-ray and limiting-law issues must be separated
obstruction: No regeneration theorem or coupling proving convergence along the wired minimal-forest ray was obtained. The preliminary one-endedness assumptions must be checked for each claimed case.
result: A bush decomposition first needs an almost surely unique infinite ray in the relevant component. Assuming that ray before proving the applicable one-endedness result would import another open assertion. Even when uniqueness is available, rooting successively along the ray is a configuration-dependent operation and does not automatically preserve the original rooted law.

independent_check: There are only countably many edges, allowing the probability-one statement to hold simultaneously for all of them. The argument uses the unique paths on Z.
method: Exact one-dimensional connectivity
obstruction: The higher-dimensional connectivity classification depends on intersections of invasion structures and is not determined by the one-dimensional calculation.
result: On Z every edge is a bridge, so the free minimal spanning forest retains all edges. For an edge with label u<1 to be excluded by a wired connection at infinity, both infinite half-lines would have to supply paths of edges with labels below u. Each such event has probability zero for iid uniform labels, since the probability for its first N edges is u^N. Thus the wired forest also retains every edge almost surely.

independent_check: For a continuous CDF that is not strictly increasing everywhere, flat intervals have zero probability of a sampled weight, so the rank argument still applies almost surely.
method: Exact universality under a monotone change of edge labels
obstruction: This is label-distribution universality on a fixed graph. It does not compare triangular and square lattice geometries or prove tightness and uniqueness of a continuum scaling limit.
result: On every finite graph with distinct edge weights, a strictly increasing transform preserves their order and hence preserves Kruskal selection and the minimum spanning tree. Independently, the cycle characterization retains exactly the same nonmaximal edges under that transform. For iid continuous distributions this identifies the law through ranks, or through the probability integral transform almost surely.

independent_check: A simple cycle in a cactus is one of its cycle blocks; there are no additional cycle constraints coupling two blocks. Continuous iid labels make every finite maximum unique almost surely.
method: Connected FMSF on trees of finite cycle blocks
obstruction: Uniformly bounded block diameters give a class roughly isometric to trees. General roughly-tree graphs can have overlapping cycles and need not admit this block decomposition.
result: Suppose an infinite cactus graph is built from bridges and edge-disjoint finite cycles. Its free minimal spanning forest retains every bridge and removes exactly the unique largest-weight edge of each cycle. Each resulting cycle block remains connected. A finite block path between any two vertices remains connected after these deletions, so the forest is globally connected and acyclic.

independent_check: Merely proving that two measures are unequal is insufficient: two different positive bounded densities relative to the same measure are still equivalent. The binary digits of Cantor-Lebesgue measure are not assumed iid.
method: Likelihood-ratio strategy and its exact missing input
obstruction: No divergent conditional-entropy estimate or martingale tail control was established for the actual harmonic measure versus base-three Cantor measure.
result: For product Bernoulli measures with different parameters, the strong law gives disjoint full-measure sets of limiting digit frequencies and hence mutual singularity. A possible analogous strategy for the two Cantor measures is a likelihood-ratio martingale along a common binary coding, with cumulative conditional relative entropy forcing its limit to vanish.

independent_check: For color zero the unconditioned masses are .30 for two mixed children (K=1), .15 for two zero children (K=2), and .05 for three zero children (K=3); divide by color probability .5. For color one the corresponding masses are .15,.30,.05. Cylinder mass is exactly the product of reciprocal K values; Fubini transfers the ray statement to almost every tree and almost every flow ray.
method: Exact dimension drop for the nonergodic same-color flow candidate
obstruction: This author-checked special construction supports dimension drop and is not a counterexample to the full question. It inherits the P0033 coloring proof and remains without independent review.
result: For the AND/OR color construction of P0033, let K be the number of children of the parent color and choose uniformly among them. Conditional on root color zero, P(K=1,2,3)=(3/5,3/10,1/10); conditional on color one it is (3/10,3/5,1/10). The full conditional-child selection lemma implies these K variables are iid along the selected ray within each color class. Hence the local dimension is h_0=(3/10)log 2+(1/10)log 3 or h_1=(3/5)log 2+(1/10)log 3 by the strong law. Both are strictly less than log(12/5), the Galton-Watson dimension.

independent_check: The two-child example is not an iid Galton-Watson tree. Its role is to disprove a pointwise local entropy monotonicity claim, not the global dimension conjecture.
method: Regular-tree equality and a local-entropy countercheck
obstruction: Global dimension averages local entropy under a bias-dependent law of the environment seen along the ray. Controlling that changing law remains necessary.
result: On a deterministic b-ary tree, symmetry makes harmonic measure uniform on children for every transient bias lambda<b, so its dimension is log b, independent of lambda. Thus strict monotonicity must exclude deterministic offspring. A local root-entropy proof also fails: attach regular trees of branching 2 and 4 as two root subtrees. Their escape probabilities are 1-lambda/2 and 1-lambda/4 for lambda<2; last-exit child probabilities are proportional to these values and become more unequal as lambda increases toward 2, so their entropy decreases.

independent_check: An elementary comparison shows the logical gap: drift at lambda=1,D=2 is 1/3, while at lambda=2,D=100 it is 98/102. Pointwise monotonicity in lambda cannot compare averages taken under different offspring laws.
method: The changing stationary environment blocks a pointwise drift proof
obstruction: The example is not a Galton-Watson speed counterexample. No sign bound for the measure-change term, or alternative monotone coupling of speeds, was proved.
result: For fixed offspring D, the radial drift (D-lambda)/(D+lambda) decreases with lambda, and on a regular tree it gives the exact speed. In a nondegenerate Galton-Watson tree the stationary distribution of the environment seen by the walker also changes with lambda, so differentiating the speed has an additional measure-change term.

method: Primary-source check of the iid finite-mean reduction
obstruction: The independent non-identically distributed bounded-length question remains unresolved here.
result: Burdzy-Scheutzow (2014), Theorem 5.1 explicitly proves that strongly decomposable processes with finite mean segment length are two-sided Brownian motions. P0028-A001 rederives this known special case and is not a novel solution.

independent_check: Both the vanishing gradient and Hessian signs were checked; the graph is connected and cubic. This is an exact deterministic obstruction to a connectivity-only proof.
method: Global Kuramoto synchronization of random cubic graphs special-case or structural calculation
obstruction: Must show that uniformly random cubic graphs avoid all such stable phase arrangements with probability tending to one; the prism family itself has vanishing probability.
result: On the cubic prism C_m times K_2, m>=5, put theta_(j,a)=2 pi j/m for both layers. The sine forces along the two cycle neighbors cancel and rung forces vanish. The Hessian is a weighted Laplacian with cycle weights cos(2 pi/m)>0 and rung weights1, so it is positive definite modulo the global rotation. This is a nonconsensus strict local minimum modulo rotation.

independent_check: The noise-average variance calculation is exact. The signal identity fails already for phases whose squares are not a common multiple of their first powers.
method: Subspectral detection from a growing number of synchronization frequencies special-case or structural calculation
obstruction: Need an algorithm exploiting algebraic relations between distinct powers. Repetition-based variance reduction solves a different experiment.
result: If L independent observations repeated the same rank-one signal, averaging would divide noise standard deviation by sqrt(L) and reduce the effective spectral threshold. In the actual model the vectors x^(k) differ with k, so averaging Y_k yields a sum of different rank-one projectors. It is not a repeated observation of xx*.

independent_check: The calculation uses the displayed matrix normalization; using unnormalized Wigner noise gives the same ratio. An oracle seed is stronger than an enumerated guessed seed.
method: Subexponential detection at fixed synchronization frequencies special-case or structural calculation
obstruction: This only defeats a one-step seed-and-average method. Iterative amplification or a different subexponential algorithm is not ruled out.
result: Try enumerating an oracle seed of m=o(n) signal coordinates and use their edges to estimate a new coordinate in one channel. After multiplying by known seed phases, the sum has signal amplitude lambda m/n and noise standard deviation sqrt(m/n), so signal-to-noise ratio is lambda sqrt(m/n), which tends to zero.

independent_check: Double-counting pairs (I,J) with symmetric difference S gives the Rayleigh coefficient. Squaring A_S toggles the same subset S twice and returns I exactly when that toggle preserves cardinality.
method: Kikuchi spectral thresholds as the polynomial degree increases special-case or structural calculation
obstruction: A Gaussian matrix-series bound introduces sqrt(log binomial(n,l)) into the norm estimate. Removing that loss and controlling the actual outlier transition remain necessary; the r=2 scope caveat needs resolution.
result: Each row has k=binomial(l,r/2)binomial(n-l,r/2) nonzero entries. For the normalized all-ones vector v, v*M(lambda)*v=lambda k+(k/binomial(n,r))sum_(|S|=r)Z_S. Thus its noise variance is k^2/binomial(n,r). Write M(0)=sum_S Z_S A_S; A_S^2 is the diagonal indicator of |I intersection S|=r/2, hence sum_S A_S^2=k I.

independent_check: The update probability of each spin may depend on its field, but at beta=0 it does not depend on neighboring spins, so agreement is preserved. This is a complete endpoint proof, with no novelty claim.
method: Polynomial Glauber mixing throughout the SK high-temperature regime special-case or structural calculation
obstruction: For beta>0 a later update can destroy agreement through neighboring disagreements. The beta=0 coupon-collector argument does not control the whole replica-symmetric interval.
result: At beta=0, spins are independent under the target product law. Couple two random-scan heat-bath chains using the same update coordinate and uniform draw. Once a coordinate has been updated it agrees forever. The probability some coordinate remains unupdated by t is at most n(1-1/n)^t<=n exp(-t/n), giving mixing time at most n log(n/epsilon) for every external field.

independent_check: Uniqueness of the simple path verifies both algorithms separately. This endpoint is included in known special cases, not a new solution.
method: Geodesic selection by reinforced ants structural argument
obstruction: Cycles permit different simple paths and histories affect their weights. The deterministic tree reduction gives no control of their competition.
result: On a finite tree with one food vertex, every N-F walk has the same simple path after loop erasure, and the shortest path in its trace is that path too. Each edge of that path therefore receives exactly one increment per ant; every other edge receives zero. The normalized weights converge to its indicator without a probabilistic limit theorem.

independent_check: The transition probability and one-increment update coincide exactly with the urn. This is a scope counterexample, not a refutation under the original restriction.
method: Deterministic limits for trace-reinforced ants structural argument
obstruction: For simple finite graphs the nonlinear trace-hitting probabilities still require a uniqueness/attraction argument. On Z^2, changing conductances additionally complicate the guarantee that every ant reaches food.
result: If two parallel edges connect N directly to F, an ant crosses exactly one and reinforces it. Starting at weights a,b gives the classical Polya urn: the first normalized weight has Beta(a,b) limit with variance ab/((a+b)^2(a+b+1))>0. Thus the unrestricted multigraph formulation is false, and the underlying no-parallel-food assumption is necessary.

independent_check: This is a pathwise implication and does not assume independence. It deliberately leaves divergence of Delta_n as an extra hypothesis.
method: Maximal degree and its location in the infinite-path fitness regime structural argument
obstruction: Neither the rate of Delta_n nor even its divergence follows from local finiteness alone. A deterministic infinite path has maximum degree2.
result: Let Delta_n be the maximum degree and I_n a maximizing label. If Delta_n tends to infinity and each fixed vertex has finite limiting degree, then I_n tends to infinity: for every fixed K, the maximum of the K finite limiting degrees is finite, and eventually Delta_n exceeds it.

independent_check: The handshaking identity proves the first statement. A star has empirical law tending to delta_1 while its empirical mean tends to2, confirming the moment caveat.
method: Empirical degree scaling for superlinear attachment with fitness structural argument
obstruction: Tightness supplies no unique limit or model-specific tail scaling. Escape of the first moment must be tracked separately.
result: For every n-vertex tree, the empirical degree law pi_n satisfies sum_k k pi_n(k)=2-2/n, hence pi_n([K,infinity))<=2/K. Thus the unscaled empirical laws are tight on the positive integers. Any weak subsequential limit is a probability law with mean at most2; its mean can be smaller because degrees are not uniformly integrable.

independent_check: The bound follows by summing nonnegative degrees; it remains valid with parallel edges and sequential updates.
method: Multiple-attachment phase transition with superlinear fitness structural argument
obstruction: A tree embedding into independent genealogical birth processes is lost when a vertex has several parents. The degree budget does not identify the phase boundary.
result: After n arrivals with exactly m outgoing attachments each, total degree is 2m(n-1) up to the finite seed. Consequently no collection of vertices can each have degree fraction greater than a if it contains more than 2m/a vertices. This bounds the number of macroscopic hubs but permits several of them, unlike a single-star conclusion.

independent_check: The conditional mean is obtained by summing x times its copying probability. Boundedness controls the martingale part without controlling the accumulated drift.
method: Fluctuations of fitness-reinforced sequence sums structural argument
obstruction: A martingale CLT alone cannot settle the question: fluctuations of Q_n/S_n and the slowly relaxing drift may contribute at the same or larger scale.
result: Writing S_n=sum X_i and Q_n=sum X_i^2 gives E[X_(n+1)|F_n]=beta m_1+(1-beta)Q_n/S_n. Subtracting this predictable mean yields bounded martingale differences, but the centered sum also contains sum[beta m_1+(1-beta)Q_i/S_i-lambda_star].

independent_check: The integral of e^(-x)x^alpha equals Gamma(alpha+1); the deduction is explicitly conditional on no escaped mass.
method: Boundary profile of the reinforced-sequence condensate structural argument
obstruction: The source provides only vague convergence away from the boundary. Finding a_n and proving boundary tightness are the load-bearing missing steps.
result: Let rho=1-beta integral (1-x)^(-1)dmu be the mass missing from the bulk limit. If the claimed rescaled measure is tight on (0,infinity) and carries all that missing mass, integrating its density forces c=rho/Gamma(alpha+1). Without those two additional controls this identification is invalid.

independent_check: For a truncation L, divide the innovation sum by n and use the iid strong law; let L increase afterward.
method: Growth of sums with unbounded reinforcement fitness structural argument
obstruction: Finite-mean unbounded mu requires amplification by reinforcement; innovation lower bounds alone remain linear and cannot give the requested rate.
result: Let K_n count innovation draws and let Y_j be their iid values. Every innovation appears at least once, so S_n>=sum_(j<=K_n)Y_j and S_n>=max_(j<=K_n)Y_j, while K_n/n tends to beta almost surely. If E_mu Y=infinity, the truncated strong law and then monotone convergence give S_n/n tending to infinity from this lower bound alone.

independent_check: All denominators equal2^alpha, so the example has no undefined 0/0 term. It does not contradict convergence from strictly positive initial counts.
method: Weak reinforcement on infinite WARM networks structural argument
obstruction: The positive-equilibrium uniqueness and stochastic attraction problem on general infinite graphs remains; no finite total Lyapunov function is available.
result: On Z with all firing rates1, set edge values alternately2 and0. At each vertex the only positive incident edge is selected with probability1; its two endpoints supply total rate2, while zero edges get rate0. This is an equilibrium for every alpha>0. Shifting gives a second one, and the uniform edge value1 is a third. Thus uniqueness among all nonnegative equilibria is false.

independent_check: Substitution in the local rate formula verifies every edge. This extends the source even-cycle observation but concerns deterministic equilibria only.
method: Critical WARM on the integer line structural argument
obstruction: Convergence to1 cannot follow merely from uniqueness of ODE equilibria, which is false. One must exploit stochastic dynamics or spatial structure to select the uniform equilibrium.
result: For any a,b>0 with a+b=2, the alternating edge configuration a,b,a,b,... solves the equilibrium equation: an a-edge receives a/(a+b) from each endpoint, totaling a, and similarly for b. Thus the ODE has a continuum of positive equilibria on the same graph.

independent_check: The equilibrium identity x_e=sum_(v~e)p_v x_e^alpha/s_v reduces the diagonal term. Multiplication by the positive diagonal x preserves the Hessian inertia of the linearized gradient flow.
method: Sharp reinforcement threshold for WARM forests structural argument
obstruction: This eliminates even cycles, not odd cycles or all odd unicyclic supports. It does not improve the universal forest threshold by itself.
result: At a positive equilibrium x, put s_v=sum_(e~v)x_e^alpha. The Hessian of the correctly rate-weighted Lyapunov function satisfies H[delta,delta]=(alpha-1)sum_e delta_e^2/x_e-alpha sum_v p_v/s_v^2 (sum_(e~v)x_e^(alpha-1)delta_e)^2. Along an even cycle choose alternating delta_e=+/-x_e^(1-alpha), zero elsewhere. Every vertex sum vanishes, giving a positive direction for alpha>1 and hence linear instability.

independent_check: The total rate of the five vertices is5, equal to2a+2b. The central vertex contributes1/2 to each equal inner edge.
method: Sharp reinforcement threshold for WARM whiskers structural argument
obstruction: Existence and stability of this scalar branch must still be analyzed, and excluding this symmetric path alone would not exclude all larger asymmetric trees.
result: Consider a support path of four edges with reflection-symmetric values a,b,b,a and unit vertex rates. The endpoint equation is a=1+a^alpha/(a^alpha+b^alpha), so 1<a<2. The neighboring inner-edge equation is b=b^alpha/(a^alpha+b^alpha)+1/2. Summing gives a+b=5/2. Thus any such equilibrium reduces to a scalar equation with b=5/2-a.

independent_check: The example computes the marginals and connectivity exactly. It is a counterexample to a marginal-only proof method, not to WARM.
method: Finite surviving components in infinite superlinear WARM structural argument
obstruction: A valid comparison needs conditional probability bounds or explicit dependence control, together with convergence of the edge weights; small one-edge probabilities are insufficient.
result: If every edge had survival probability at most q, this would not imply domination by iid Bernoulli percolation. For example, activate all edges simultaneously with probability q and none otherwise. Every marginal is q, yet there is an infinite component with probability q for every q>0 on an infinite connected graph.

independent_check: This is the exponential-versus-polynomial volume comparison, independent of reinforcement details.
method: WARM percolation with vanishing rates on lattices structural argument
obstruction: Unbounded subdivisions change the local competition and rates along paths. The volume obstruction explains why a direct bounded-distortion transfer fails but does not exclude lattice WARM percolation.
result: There is no bounded-length embedding of a b-ary tree, b>=2, into Z^d with distinct vertices: its depth-r ball contains order b^r vertices, whereas images lie in a lattice ball of radius Lr with only O(r^d) vertices. Therefore transferring the known regular-tree construction requires unbounded subdivisions or a different geometry.

independent_check: This is the standard gambler-ruin proof of the constant-weight case, not a new result. Constant weights satisfy the stated sublinear condition for any alpha in(0,1).
method: Recurrence of sublinear vertex-reinforced walk on Z structural argument
obstruction: For nonconstant reinforcement, position alone is not Markov and the gambler-ruin harmonic function no longer solves the conditional transition equation.
result: For constant w the walk is simple symmetric random walk. Starting at1 and stopping at0 or m, the harmonic function h(k)=k/m gives probability1/m of hitting m before0. Letting m tend to infinity shows that the probability of avoiding0 forever is0; by the strong Markov property returns recur indefinitely.

independent_check: The proof needs no conditional independence. The strong law follows from summable variances of martingale increments divided by n, then Kronecker. The maximum principle can also be checked by propagating the set of zero coordinates backwards through irreducibility.
method: Forced network urn convergence and diffusion scaling structural argument
obstruction: This resolves the fixed-step convergence subquestion under the stated assumptions, but not the whole diffusion question. Fast synchronization, an initial layer, and the covariance specification must be treated before a full solution label.
result: A complete fixed-step classification follows. On any event Z_n->z, the update forces X_n to converge to a binary vector x and hence eventually equal it. The bounded martingale-difference strong law gives x=Qz. The update limit gives z=(r x+f p)/(r+f). A binary coordinate of Qz can equal0 or1 only when all its positive-weight predecessors have the same x-value and matching p-value. Irreducibility then forces x and p to be the all-zero or all-one vector. Conversely if p=0, the positive stationary vector pi gives E[pi.Z_n]=(1-f)^n E[pi.Z_0], and Markov plus Borel-Cantelli yields Z_n->0; p=1 follows by complementing.

independent_check: Use sum p_i^2<=max p_i sum p_i. This verifies the count approximation only; the vertex targets retain degree-dependent marks.
method: Matching local limits of Bernoulli and Poisson-outdegree attachment structural argument
obstruction: A matching outgoing count does not prove local graph convergence. Target choices, ancestor types, and dependencies across successive births must be coupled over an explored neighborhood.
result: Conditional on current degrees, the Bernoulli outgoing count has mean Lambda_n=sum_i p_ni. Its total variation distance to Poisson(Lambda_n) is at most sum_i p_ni^2 by the elementary independent Bernoulli-to-Poisson coupling. If max_i p_ni->0 and Lambda_n stays bounded, this error tends to0.

independent_check: Markov gives P(deg(U_n)>K)<=2m/K+o(1) without assumptions on f.
method: Local limits for nonaffine attachment with multiple edges structural argument
obstruction: Tightness of the root degree alone does not ensure tightness of radius-two neighborhoods: a uniformly selected leaf can attach to a hub of diverging degree. Condensation and size bias must be controlled.
result: With m=1 and equal attachment weights, the graph is a uniform recursive tree and its empirical degree law is tight by the tree degree identity. With m>=2 the degree budget still gives uniform-root degree tightness, since its mean is at most2m plus a vanishing seed term.

independent_check: Jordan normal form shows M^n->0 when its spectral radius is below1, including reducible matrices.
method: Multistate pivot-tree criterion for interpretation structural argument
obstruction: At spectral radius1 the first moment need not decay, and reducible type classes can behave differently. The established subcritical argument does not settle critical/supercritical interpretation.
result: For a finite-type pivot branching process with mean matrix M and spectral radius less than1, E[population at level n] tends to0, hence P(level n nonempty)<=E[size] tends to0. This proves extinction and explains the subcritical direction already covered by Theorem1.8.

independent_check: The population is exactly one at every level. The top-left K by K shift matrix has Kth power zero.
method: Infinite-state tree-automaton interpretation criteria structural argument
obstruction: Finite truncations falsely suggest extinction because population escapes through types. Any infinite-state criterion needs tightness or a suitable operator topology, not only finite truncation eigenvalues.
result: Consider a countable-type branching process in which each type k individual has deterministically one child of type k+1. It survives forever, although every finite truncation of its mean matrix is nilpotent and every fixed type eventually disappears.

independent_check: Conditional variance given the bare tree is p(1-p)>0; conditional variance given innovations is0.
method: Randomized tree automata and endogeny structural argument
obstruction: A literal extension retaining only the unmarked-tree sigma-field is false. A useful theorem must specify the innovation sigma-field and then handle nontrivial child dependence.
result: Let each vertex state be its own independent Bernoulli(p) innovation, ignoring its children. The pivot tree is empty and the state is measurable from the marked tree, but for 0<p<1 it is independent of the unmarked tree and cannot be a measurable function of that tree.

independent_check: For example, the algebraic system x-y=0 in a square has a whole line of zeros; this illustrates the logical gap without asserting that this system comes from an automaton.
method: Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton structural argument
obstruction: The nonnegative multinomial coefficients and deterministic count assignments constrain which algebraic sets can occur. Neither an admissible positive-dimensional example nor a general exclusion is obtained.
result: If the offspring distribution has finite support bounded by D, each coordinate of the distributional map is a polynomial of degree at most D in the color probabilities. Fixed points are therefore a compact real algebraic subset of the probability simplex. In contrast with one variable, polynomial equations may have curves of zeros, so analyticity alone cannot prove finiteness.

independent_check: This is the intermediate value theorem and the derivative sign at a simple root; it makes no claim for tangencies or nondifferentiable maps.
method: Prescribing rogue and interpretable automaton fixed points structural argument
obstruction: The derivative restriction is necessary, not sufficient for an automaton realization or rogue classification in degenerate cases. Constructing compatible multinomial maps remains open here.
result: For a differentiable increasing distributional map Psi, let g(p)=Psi(p)-p. At an isolated simple fixed point, crossing from g>0 to g<0 gives Psi prime<1, while the opposite crossing gives Psi prime>1. Consecutive simple interior crossings must alternate signs. Thus a prescribed list of simple attractive/repulsive crossings cannot have two consecutive crossings of the same orientation without an intervening zero.

independent_check: The relevant set must be fixed independently of the child configuration; a pointwise bound on pivotal children alone would not justify this global coupling. For symmetric count automata the crude k(D)=D criterion reduces to E D<1.
method: Automaton-level conditions for a unique fixed point structural argument
obstruction: For supercritical offspring the crude contraction constant exceeds1. A useful structural criterion must exploit much finer properties than the number of children.
result: Suppose that for each offspring count D the rule depends on a fixed set of at most k(D) child positions, and E k(D)=c<1. Couple child colors optimally with disagreement probability dTV(mu,nu); the union bound over that fixed relevant set gives dTV(Psi(mu),Psi(nu))<=c dTV(mu,nu). Iteration is a contraction and yields a unique fixed point on the finite simplex.

independent_check: Finite approximate minimizing paths establish continuity without geodesic existence. Cox-Kesten continuity cited in the primary simulation paper gives a second route. Each actual epsilon-law has no zero atom and has positive time constant.
method: Supercritical zero-weight limit and bounded finite-distance continuity
obstruction: No mathematical gap identified in the written candidate; later-literature and erratum search remain incomplete. No explicit numerical epsilon threshold or independent review is claimed.
result: Take tau=eta+epsilon U with P(eta=0)=3/4 and U uniform[0,1]. For epsilon>0 this is atomless and bounded with F(0)=0. The four-edge minimum has expectation at least1/256. The eta-model time constant is0. For each n, passage times converge to their eta-model values and are bounded by2n; dominated convergence and mu=inf_n E T(0,ne1)/n imply mu_epsilon tends to0. All sufficiently small epsilon reverse the proposed inequality.

independent_check: Solve (3/4)t/epsilon=2/3 to obtain8epsilon/9. Compute16/(9*1024)=1/576. The expected minimum bound comes from the all-four-expensive event of probability1/256. The earlier continuity proof independently gives the qualitative family.
method: Primary theorem comparison and exact quantile evaluation
obstruction: No current-open problem remains for this universal inequality. This is literature-established, not an original solution.
result: Ahlberg2019/2020 already refuted the question. Applying his mu<=2t_(2/3) to the independently drafted tau=eta+epsilon U family gives t_(2/3)=8epsilon/9, hence mu<=16epsilon/9. With epsilon=1/1024, mu<=1/576<1/256<=E minfour. This supplies an explicit atomless bounded counterexample using an established theorem.

independent_check: The equality holds configuration by configuration before taking any limit. Positive-time and nondegeneracy restrictions exclude the zero-time percolation examples.
method: An explicit nontrivial FPP time constant and limit shape structural argument
obstruction: Homogeneity supplies a transformation law, not a computable nondegenerate base model. Integrable directed last-passage formulas apply to a different optimization problem.
result: If every edge time is multiplied by c>0, every finite path cost and every passage time is multiplied by c, so the time constant is multiplied by c and the limit shape is dilated by1/c. Thus scaling a known degenerate example cannot produce the missing nontrivial shape.

independent_check: The bound does not depend on a minimizing path or an upper bound on its length. It proves an actual strict gap for this special stochastic ordering.
method: Strict FPP comparison in higher dimensions at a large minimum atom structural argument
obstruction: General increasing-concave order, including mean-preserving spreads, has no pointwise additive coupling. The argument does not handle the remaining comparison class.
result: For the special coupling tau'_e=tau_e+delta with delta>0, every path from0 to ne1 has at least n edges. Its primed cost is at least its original cost plus delta n. Taking infima and limits gives mu'(e1)>=mu(e1)+delta.

independent_check: The inequality ||x||_infinity <= ||x||_p <= d^(1/p)||x||_infinity verifies the convergence directly.
method: Strict convexity of iid FPP limit shapes structural argument
obstruction: This is a counterexample to an inference about limits, not an iid FPP counterexample. A uniform quantitative gap in the triangle inequality is missing.
result: Finite geodesic uniqueness does not imply strict convexity of an asymptotic norm. For example, the strictly convex norms ||x||_p converge uniformly on compact sets to ||x||_infinity as p tends to infinity, and the latter unit ball has flat faces. Even stronger finite approximations can lose strictness in the limit.

independent_check: Both balls are compact with nonempty interior and invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes. Their intersections with the supporting plane x1=1 distinguish the facet from the corner.
method: Excluding axial facets and cubical FPP shapes structural argument
obstruction: One needs a property specific to iid optimization that excludes the cubical candidate; deterministic convex geometry alone supplies none.
result: The l_infinity unit ball satisfies every elementary symmetry and convexity condition of an FPP limit shape and has axial facets. The l1 unit ball also satisfies those conditions but has an axial corner. Thus the shape theorem's convexity and lattice symmetries permit both geometries.

independent_check: The lower bound is pathwise. Along an oriented path, its length equals the l1 displacement, so equality is exact.
method: Classification of flat FPP boundary pieces structural argument
obstruction: The mechanism proves why these flats occur, not why no alternative mechanism creates a flat segment away from that cone.
result: If tau_e>=1, then every path from0 to x costs at least ||x||_1, so the limit shape lies inside the l1 ball. An oriented path consisting entirely of unit-time edges attains this lower bound exactly. This explains the mechanism generating the known cone flats.
